description: EXIT PARAGRAPH (ISO §2023:14.9.14.2 Format 4 / §2023:14.9.14.4 GR6) — a COBOL-2002 structured-procedure exit transferring control to the implicit CONTINUE at the end of the current paragraph. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 Nucleus EXIT statement's general format is the bare word `EXIT` (§1985:VI.6.14.2), and §1985:VI.6.14.3 SR1 reads 'The EXIT statement must appear only in a sentence by itself and comprise the only sentence in the paragraph' (§1985:VI.6.14.4 GR1: 'An EXIT statement serves only to enable the user to assign a procedure-name to a given point in a program'); its one other EXIT is the Inter-Program Communication EXIT PROGRAM (§1985:X.5.4.1: 'The EXIT PROGRAM statement marks the logical end of a called program'). §2002:14.8.13 adds Format 5 `EXIT PERFORM [ CYCLE ]` and Format 6 `EXIT { PARAGRAPH | SECTION }`: 'The EXIT PERFORM statement provides a means of exiting an inline PERFORM (with or without returning to any specified test)' and 'The EXIT PARAGRAPH and EXIT SECTION statements provide a means of exiting a structured procedure without executing any of the following statements within the procedure', and §2002:F.2 states the change, its item 49: 'The ability to immediately exit an inline PERFORM statement, a paragraph, or a section has been added.' §2002:14.8.13.3 GR11: 'The execution of an EXIT PARAGRAPH statement causes control to be passed to an implicit CONTINUE statement immediately following the last explicit statement of the current paragraph'. §2014:14.9.13.3 GR11 prints the 2002 rule unchanged, so 2014 = 2023 (2023 adds SR10, 'The EXIT statement with the PARAGRAPH phrase may be specified only in a paragraph').
vcr: 2002 introduction (§2002:14.8.13 Format 6; §2002:F.2 item 49; no VCR row)
